correctness.rationale: The two-neighbor fixed-condition is an iff; five/six exact allowed page pairs yield coefficient formulas. For opposing hubs, the dominant two marginal nonretention events have a three-valued random-walk tail; competing-color outcomes have exponential base beta=(2+2sqrt(3))/6<rho, and joint nonretention has base mu=(2r+r^2+2+r^-2)/6<rho. Exponential tilting and aperiodic lattice local CLT prove tail c*rho^m/sqrt(m) with correct lattice prefactor r/(1-r), and agreeing-hub states are bounded by 3*5^m, smaller than correction base 1+2sqrt(6). Independent dynamic-programming and vertex-level brute force scripts agree on all labelled states for m=1..5; exact recurrence checks extend through m=10. The proof, not experiments, is all-size.

value.rationale: The natural family of edge-glued quadrilateral books has a hub-edge bottleneck and arbitrarily many labelled pages. The theorem identifies and explains a counterintuitive hub-opinion separation among fixed states, determines the exact all-size stationary-state enumeration and an explicit nontrivial first missing-mass correction with algebraic exponential rate (1+2sqrt6) and m^-1/2 prefactor. These observables distinguish tie-retaining local influence from best response and are not routine finite tabulations. No general long-term convergence claim is made.
